title: Verb + preposition 1: to and at
subtitle: listen to / look at
summary: Learn which verbs take to, which take at, and which take no preposition at all - and how shout at and shout to differ.

lesson.heading: talk to, listen to, apologise to
lesson.text: We say **talk / speak to** somebody (talk with is also possible), **listen to** something and **apologise to** somebody (for something).

examples.text: When I'm driving, I like to **listen to** the radio.
They **apologised to** me for their mistake.

lesson.heading: explain / describe something to somebody
lesson.text: We **explain something to** somebody and **describe something to** somebody. The person always comes after **to**.

examples.text: I **explained to** them why I was worried.
Let me **describe to** you what I saw.

lesson.heading: Verbs with no preposition
lesson.text: Some verbs take the person straight after them: **phone / call / email / text** somebody, **answer** somebody or something, **ask** somebody (a question), **thank** somebody (for something).

examples.text: I **called the airline** to cancel my flight.
If there's anything you want to know, you can **ask me**.

lesson.note: But we say **write (a letter) to** somebody and **reply to** an email or a letter.

lesson.heading: look at, laugh at, point at
lesson.text: We say **look / stare / glance at**, **have a look / take a look at**, **laugh at**, **aim / point (something) at** and **shoot / fire (a gun) at**.

examples.text: Why are you **looking at** me like that?
I look stupid with this haircut. Everybody will **laugh at** me.
Don't **point** that knife **at** me. It's dangerous.
We saw someone with a gun **shooting at** birds, but he didn't hit any.

lesson.heading: shout at or shout to? throw at or throw to?

left.label: at = aggressive, or trying to hit
examples: He got very angry and started **shouting at** me.

right.label: to = so they can hear or catch
examples: He **shouted to** me from the other side of the street.
Lisa shouted 'Catch!' and **threw** the keys **to** me from the window.

lesson.text: Two mistakes to avoid: never say ~~listen the radio~~ or ~~explain me something~~ - it's listen **to** the radio and explain something **to** me.

exercises.prompt: When I'm driving, I like to listen ___ the radio.
exercises.explanation: Listen always takes to before an object.

options: They apologised to me for their mistake.
They apologised me for their mistake.
They apologised for me their mistake.
exercises.explanation: We apologise to somebody for something.

exercises.prompt: I glanced ___ my watch to see what time it was.
exercises.explanation: Look, stare and glance all take at.

exercises.statement: My friend texted to me to let me know she was going to be late.
exercises.explanation: My friend texted me. Phone, call, email and text take no preposition.

exercises.prompt: We live in the same building, but we've never ___ one another.
exercises.explanation: Speak to or talk to somebody.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of the sentences.

exercises.prompt: It was a difficult question. I couldn't ___.
exercises.explanation: Answer takes no preposition (but we reply to something).

exercises.prompt: I tried to contact Tina, but she didn't ___ my emails.
exercises.explanation: We answer an email but we reply to an email.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition does each verb need before its object?

exercises.statement: I need somebody to explain me what I have to do.
exercises.explanation: I need somebody to explain to me what I have to do.

exercises.prompt: If you don't want that sandwich, throw it ___ the birds. They'll eat it.
exercises.explanation: Throw something to somebody so that they can take or catch it.

exercises.prompt: She was so angry she threw a book ___ the wall.
exercises.explanation: Throw something at something when you want to hit it.
